conceptCapsule.title: Foundations of Dynamics: Inertia, Force & Translational Equilibrium
conceptCapsule.summary: Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia) asserts that an object continues in its state of rest or of uniform rectilinear motion unless acted upon by a net external unbalanced force ($\sum \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0} \iff \vec{a} = \vec{0}$). Inertial mass is the quantitative measure of translational inertia. Inertia manifests in three distinct physical forms: (1) Inertia of rest, (2) Inertia of motion, and (3) Inertia of direction. An inertial reference frame is one in which Newton's first law holds valid without introducing fictitious pseudo-forces.
conceptCapsule.examTrap: Never confuse an equilibrium pair of forces (e.g., normal force and weight on a resting book, which act on the same body) with a Newton's third law action-reaction pair (which always act on two distinct interacting bodies). Remember that in uniform circular motion, speed is constant but velocity is not—hence by Newton's first law, a net external centripetal force is mandatory to sustain circular curvature.

questions.statement: Newton's first law of motion gives the qualitative definition of:
questions.solution:
Newton's first law defines the intrinsic resistance of matter to changes in velocity (Inertia) and qualitatively defines Force as the external cause capable of altering that state of rest or uniform motion.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: The quantitative measure of inertia of a body in rectilinear motion is its:
questions.solution:
In translational mechanics, mass ($m$) is the quantitative measure of inertia. A larger mass requires a proportionally larger force to achieve a given acceleration.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A passenger in a moving bus is thrown forward when the bus suddenly stops. This phenomenon is an example of:
questions.solution:
When the bus brakes suddenly, the passenger's feet come to rest with the vehicle via friction, while the upper torso continues moving forward due to inertia of motion.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A person sitting in an open train compartment travelling with uniform velocity tosses a ball vertically upwards. The ball falls:

options.text: To the left of his hand

questions.solution:
In an inertial frame moving with constant velocity, the ball retains the horizontal velocity of the train throughout flight ($a_x = 0$), landing precisely back in the thrower's hand.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In the previous scenario, if the train accelerates forward with constant acceleration $a$ while the ball is in air, the ball lands:
questions.solution:
During the flight time $T$, the ball covers $x_{\text{ball}} = v_0 T$, whereas the accelerating passenger covers $x_{\text{man}} = v_0 T + \frac{1}{2}aT^2$. Since $x_{\text{man}} > x_{\text{ball}}$, the ball falls behind his hand.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: When a wet dog shakes its body violently to dry its fur, water drops fly off tangent to the motion. This occurs primarily due to:
questions.solution:
When fur rapidly changes direction during shaking, the water droplets continue along their instantaneous tangential straight-line velocity due to inertia of direction.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A frame of reference attached to which of the following systems can be considered strictly non-inertial?

options.text: A train moving at constant speed along a straight track
A space capsule drifting in deep interstellar space with engines off
An elevator descending with constant velocity
A rotating carousel with constant angular velocity

questions.solution:
A rotating carousel possesses a non-zero centripetal acceleration ($a_c = \omega^2 r$) directed towards the axis of rotation, making it an accelerated (non-inertial) frame.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A book of mass $m$ rests on a flat table. The normal contact force exerted by the table on the book and the weight of the book:

options.text: Are equal and opposite forces acting on the same body (Equilibrium pair)
Form a Newton's third law action-reaction pair

questions.solution:
Action-reaction pairs act on different bodies. Here, the normal force (table on book) and gravity (Earth on book) act on the same body, summing to zero to satisfy Newton's first law for static equilibrium.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ is acted upon by three coplanar concurrent forces $\vec{F}_1 = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j})\text{ N}$, $\vec{F}_2 = (-5\hat{i} + \hat{j})\text{ N}$, and $\vec{F}_3$. If the particle remains in uniform motion with constant velocity $\vec{v} = (4\hat{i} - 2\hat{j})\text{ m/s}$, the force $\vec{F}_3$ must be:
questions.solution:
Constant velocity implies zero acceleration ($\vec{a} = \vec{0}$). By Newton's first law: $$\sum \vec{F} = \vec{F}_1 + \vec{F}_2 + \vec{F}_3 = \vec{0} \implies (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}) + (-5\hat{i} + \hat{j}) + \vec{F}_3 = \vec{0} \implies \vec{F}_3 = 3\hat{i} - 4\hat{j}\text{ N}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: An astronaut in free interstellar space away from any gravitational influence is traveling at $1000\text{ m/s}$. To keep moving at this constant speed in a straight line, the engine thrust required is:
questions.solution:
According to Newton's first law, no force is required to sustain uniform straight-line motion in a field-free vacuum.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A heavy block is suspended from a rigid ceiling by a string $A$, and an identical string $B$ is attached to the bottom of the block. If a sudden sharp jerk is given to string $B$:

options.text: String $B$ breaks first due to the inertia of rest of the block

questions.solution:
Due to the large inertia of rest of the heavy block, the sudden impulse does not transmit instantaneously to string $A$. The tension in string $B$ exceeds its breaking limit first.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: In the previous question, if string $B$ is pulled gradually and steadily with a continuously increasing force:

options.text: String $A$ breaks first because tension in $A$ equals weight plus applied force

questions.solution:
Under slow pulling, quasi-static equilibrium applies: $T_A = mg + F_{\text{pull}}$ while $T_B = F_{\text{pull}}$. Because $T_A > T_B$ at all times, string $A$ snaps first.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Dust is removed from a hanging carpet by beating it with a stick. The physical law underlying this technique is:

options.text: Law of conservation of linear momentum

questions.solution:
Beating sets the carpet fibres into rapid motion, while dust particles remain behind due to inertia of rest and detach.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ moves along a circular path of radius $R$ at constant speed $v$. The net external force acting on the particle is:
questions.solution:
Continuous directional change creates a centripetal acceleration $a_c = v^2/R$ directed towards the center. Hence, a net centripetal force $F = mv^2/R$ towards the center is required.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A body is in translatory equilibrium when:

options.text: Its kinetic energy is strictly zero
Its acceleration is directed towards a fixed point
The vector sum of all external forces acting on it is zero ($\sum \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}$)

questions.solution:
Translational equilibrium requires $\vec{a}_{\text{cm}} = \vec{0}$, which holds if and only if $\sum \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: When an automobile negotiates a sharp curve to the left, passengers experience an outward push towards the right. This perceived push is due to:

options.text: Inertia of direction (tendency to continue in a straight line)

questions.solution:
Passengers tend to maintain their original straight-line trajectory due to inertia of direction, causing a relative outward displacement with respect to the turning vehicle.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding inertial frames of reference?

options.text: Newton's first law is valid in all inertial frames
A frame rotating with uniform angular velocity relative to an inertial frame is also inertial
Any frame moving with constant velocity relative to an inertial frame is inertial
A fictitious pseudo-force is not required in an inertial frame

questions.solution:
A rotating frame experiences centripetal acceleration ($-\omega^2\vec{r}$) and is therefore non-inertial.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $M$ is placed on a frictionless horizontal plane. A light string attached to the block passes over a frictionless pulley and carries a suspended mass $m$. The net force causing the acceleration of the entire combined system is:
questions.solution:
For the whole system of mass $(M + m)$, normal force balances $Mg$, and internal string tension cancels out. The sole unbalanced driving force is gravity on the hanging mass, $F_{\text{ext}} = mg$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A bird is sitting in a large airtight glass cage held by a person. If the bird starts flying with uniform velocity inside the cage, the weight of the cage felt by the person:
questions.solution:
To fly with uniform velocity, the bird must push air downward with a thrust equal to its weight $mg$. In an airtight cage, this downward air thrust is transmitted to the cage bottom, keeping the scale reading unchanged.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: Three concurrent forces $\vec{F}_1 = 6\text{ N}$ (East), $\vec{F}_2 = 8\text{ N}$ (North), and $\vec{F}_3$ keep a particle in static equilibrium. The magnitude and direction of $\vec{F}_3$ are:
questions.solution:
1. $\vec{F}_{12} = 6\hat{i} + 8\hat{j} \implies |\vec{F}_{12}| = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10\text{ N}$.
2. For static equilibrium: $\vec{F}_3 = -\vec{F}_{12} = -6\hat{i} - 8\hat{j}$.
3. Magnitude $= 10\text{ N}$, Direction: $\tan\theta = \frac{8}{6} = \frac{4}{3}$ West of South.
Therefore, Option A is correct.
